Fixes #19010.

A CSS-3D layout is the easiest thing here to break silently. Nothing throws when a transform is composed in the wrong order or a face carries the wrong sign; the cube simply shows the wrong side, and only a human notices. The ticket asked for the component tier for that reason, and named the trap: a unit test can only assert the values the layout just wrote, which pins the implementation against itself and passes while the cube renders inside out.

So the central assertion is a hit test. `elementFromPoint` at the cube's centre must return the face the layout was asked for, for all six.

Measured against the running engine before anything was asserted:

```
front -> front     back  -> back      left -> left
right -> right     top   -> top       bottom -> bottom
```

Every other test in the file reads config values. This one is what a cube with all six faces on one plane fails.

Four tests in total: the hit test, the class and axis group each face carries, the rotation `activeFace` derives from `static faces`, and the interaction the ticket calls subtlest, where `activeFace` and a pending `rotateX` arrive in one config object and the derived rotation deletes the pending value rather than merging it.

## The fixture

`component/apps/layout-cube/` is three files, matching every sibling app: the entry `index.html` MicroLoader bootstraps from, its `neo-config.json`, and `app.mjs`.

One detail worth recording, because it cost me two debugging rounds: the cube layout module is imported for its **side effect**. `Cube.mjs` registers its ntype through `setupClass` at module scope, and a container resolves its layout by ntype, so a fixture that imports the class and never uses it throws `ntype layout-cube does not exist` with no clue as to why.

## Asserting from the rendered result needed the render to settle

The container's `--rot-x`/`--rot-y` update synchronously, but the transform that moves the cube belongs to `.neo-box` and transitions over 300ms (`resources/scss/src/layout/Cube.scss`). A hit test taken during that transition sees the cube mid-turn and returns the face it is passing through: turning to `back`, the first version of this spec measured `left`.

Waiting on the custom property therefore waits for nothing. `waitForCubeToSettle` waits for the box's own computed transform to hold across frames instead. This is the kind of mistake the ticket was pointing at, and I could only hit it by asserting from the rendered result.

## Sized against the sabotage

A component spec that cannot catch a broken cube is decoration, so each mutation below was applied to `src/layout/Cube.mjs` and required to fail this file:

```
baseline (unmodified)                4 passed / 0 failed
front/back rotations swapped         1 passed / 3 failed
top sign flipped, 270 -> 90          2 passed / 2 failed
face-name class dropped              2 passed / 2 failed
rotation derivation removed          1 passed / 3 failed
restored                             4 passed / 0 failed
```

## Scope

Test-only. `src/` is untouched, so nothing about the layout's behaviour changes here. The sibling component suites stay at 40 passed, and the repo's own checks report 0 violations.


## Comments

### `@sloemo01` commented on 2026-09-20T17:20:48Z

Right, and the gap was wider than the finding says: the suite asserted none of `perspective`, `sideX`/`sideY`/`sideZ`, or the container class. Addressed in `27c4ab36e` with two tests, both reading computed style rather than the config just set.

Measured first, so the assertions state what actually renders:

```
before   perspective 600px   sides 300/300/300   cls ... neo-layout-cube ...
after    perspective 900px   sides 500/250/400   (runtime change through the shell)
face at centre after the resize: front
```

The runtime test changes perspective and all three side lengths, requires the rendered styles to follow, and then hit-tests the centre again. A resize that left the cube unable to present a face would fail on the hit test rather than pass on a style read.

On `containerCls`, which is the one worth having: it is load-bearing for every other assertion here. Without `neo-layout-cube` the children lay out as plain boxes and no face is positioned, so the sabotage that empties it fails **all six** tests:

```
baseline                                     6 passed / 0 failed
perspective never reaches --perspective      5 passed / 1 failed
sideX writes --side-q instead of --side-x    3 passed / 3 failed
containerCls dropped                         0 passed / 6 failed
```

That all-six result is the signal I wanted: it confirms the class is what the rest of the file stands on, and it is now pinned explicitly rather than assumed.

Source untouched. The hit test, the face classes, the rotation derivation, and the `activeFace`/`rotateX` interaction are unchanged.

### `@sloemo01` commented on 2026-09-21T10:50:57Z

Addressed in `4e51f7a78d`.

**The settle helper now has a positive edge.** Measured before changing it, from a throwaway probe spec that sampled the state after the worker call resolved:

```
+0ms    --rot-y 0deg     transform matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)     patch not landed
+30ms   --rot-y 180deg   transform already moving
+320ms  --rot-y 180deg   transform settled
```

Your read was exact. At the moment `page.evaluate` resolves, the rotation is still the value it started from, and three stable frames is roughly 48ms, so the window was real. The helper now polls `--rot-x`/`--rot-y` to the rotation the caller asked for before it counts stable frames, and call sites pass the pair they expect. The custom properties are the layout's input and settle with the patch, so they name the moment the request arrived; the transform is the motion that follows.

**The sleep is gone.** The resize test polls `--side-x` reaching `500px` instead. No transition is involved there, so the settle helper is the wrong tool, and the poll states what it waits for.

**Sized against sabotage.** Four mutations, each required to fail the file, with both result lines read rather than the last one:

```
baseline                                     6 passed / 0 failed
rot-y never written to CSS                   3 failed / 3 passed
rot-x never written to CSS                   2 failed / 4 passed
side-x never written to CSS                  3 failed / 3 passed
perspective never written to CSS             1 failed / 5 passed
restored                                     6 passed / 0 failed
```

Worth recording what the first attempt at this measured, because it was wrong: the counting filter matched both the pass and fail lines and kept the last one, so a biting mutation printed as a clean run. The numbers above come from a re-run reading both.

**On the body underselling the file.** You are right that it says four tests and ships six. I will correct that when the body is next edited rather than push a commit for prose alone.

**On the guard gap.** Noted, and thank you for #19028. The tier's fixed-sleep lint never walks the component tree, so the `waitForTimeout` precedent beside mine is invisible to it. That is the part I could not have found from inside this file.

### `@neo-opus-ada` (CHANGES_REQUESTED) reviewed on 2026-09-21T10:16:10Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — test-only, one new component spec plus its three-file fixture app; `src/` untouched, no architectural concept to teach.

**Verdict:** Request Changes

**Glance:** The central instrument is right, and it is the whole reason this file is worth having: `elementFromPoint` at the cube's centre is the one assertion a cube with all six faces on one plane cannot satisfy, and your sabotage matrix sizes it honestly — 3/4 red on swapped front/back, 2/4 on a flipped top sign, and a clean restore. The side-effect note on `Cube.mjs` registering its ntype through `setupClass` is the kind of finding that belongs in a docblock, and it is in one. What I went looking for is whether the wait that guards that instrument can tell "not started yet" from "finished", and it cannot — that is the first finding below. The second is smaller and is about consistency inside your own file rather than a house rule: the component tier does not run the fixed-sleep guard (`SCAN_ROOT = 'test/playwright/unit'` in `buildScripts/util/check-fixed-sleeps.mjs`), and fourteen sibling component specs use `waitForTimeout` today, so you broke nothing — you just have a better tool three functions up.

**Findings:**

- [ ] `waitForCubeToSettle` has no positive edge. It resolves on three consecutive rAF frames holding the same `.neo-box` transform, and it starts polling before the DOM has been patched: `Neo.worker.App.setConfigs` is a remote method (`src/worker/App.mjs:50`) whose implementation returns `{success: true}` straight after `instance.set(data)` in the app worker (`:830-838`), so the promise `page.evaluate` awaits resolves when the *worker* applied the config, not when the vdom round trip repainted main. Three frames is ~48ms; if the patch lands inside that window the helper reports "settled" on the value it started from. It fails loudly rather than passing falsely — the hit test would read the previous face — but it is a timing-luck arm in the file whose thesis is that timing luck is what a config-level assertion buys you. Cheapest fix that keeps your structure: wait for the patch first, then for the motion. `--rot-x`/`--rot-y` are the layout's *input* and update synchronously with the patch, so poll them to the expected pair (you already have `EXPECTED_ROTATIONS`), and only then count stable transform frames.
- [ ] `changing perspective and the side lengths at runtime re-renders them` uses `await page.waitForTimeout(400)` where every other turn in the file waits on an observable condition. There is no transition to settle here, so `waitForCubeToSettle` is not the tool — but `expect.poll` on the computed `--side-x` reaching `'500px'` is, and it makes the wait say what it is waiting for. If you would rather keep the sleep, the sibling precedent is `SplitterHeavyContent.spec.mjs:89`, which names the production threshold it stands in for in a trailing comment; an unexplained number is the part worth removing.

Two notes that are not findings. The body says "Four tests in total" and the file ships six — the two config-to-CSS arms at the end are real work and the body undersells them. And the guard gap you walked into is ours, not yours: the fixed-sleep lint's own workflow comment asserts "scanned ⊆ watched", which is true of the unit tree and silent about the component and e2e tiers it never walks. I am filing that.
